# read_C: pp. 69–71, plus p. 72 ll. 1–2 (leaves n70–n73), established from the images

Line counts: p. 69 has five lines (a leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔, both ༔ clear). p. 70 has five lines (a leaf back, no ornament; checked). p. 71 has five lines (a leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔, both ༔ clear). From p. 72 (a leaf back, no ornament), only lines 1–2 are given. That makes 17 print lines.
The witness's line breaks match the print on every line read (17 of 17). Witness lines 1–15 are pp. 69–71, and lines 16–17 are 72.1–72.2.

**End of the part.** No ༔ on 71.5 closes a sentence. The only one there is …འཐིབ་པའི་དབུས་སུ༔, and that ༔ comes mid-clause. The line ends …པདྨ་གར་གྱི་དབང་ཕྱུག་ཞེས་ | 72.1 བྱ་བ༔. So, as the brief says, I read on into p. 72. The description of Padma Gar gyi dbang phyug runs over the ༔s at ལྡན་པ༔, འཁྲིལ་བ༔ and ཅིང་༔. It closes at the first finite ending on **72.2: …ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ནམ་མཁའ་ལ་མཛད་པ་ཅིག་འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༔**. The part stops there, after འོང་ངོ༔. The next sentence, the eastern knowledge-holder (དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་དེའི་ཤར་ནས་ས་ལ་གནས་པའི་རིག་འཛིན…), starts mid-line on 72.2. As in part 005, the whole of 72.1 and 72.2 is transcribed.
If the editor prefers to end on a page line, the last sentence end before p. 72 is on 71.4 (…འོད་ལྔ་ཁྲ་བོ་འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ་༔). That point would split the day-seven greeting from the first vidyādhara.

Method: line bands were located from the row profile (dense rows n70 ≈140/197/253/312/368, n71 ≈146/203/256/318/370, n72 ≈135/196/253/311/374, n73 ≈142/192). The lines slope by up to about 25 px across the page, so bands were re-cut locally where needed. Each line was cropped in four overlapping segments at ×3 (LANCZOS). Doubtful syllables were cropped at ×5–×10, with pixel dumps (threshold 128) for letter shapes and tshegs.
The tshegs in this scan are mostly fused to neighbouring head bars: a connected-component search found only 31 free-standing tshegs on all of n71. A tsheg was therefore judged absent only where the letters touch or there is visibly no room for one. Each line end was checked against the right frame by pixel dump. Each ༔ after ང/ངོ was checked at ×7–×10.

| 70.2 | འབྱིང → འབྲིང | ×8: under བ there is one short vertical with a foot turned left (ra-btags). It is not the two-pronged ya-btags of བྱོན (69.2). "Middling [practitioners]". The other recension has འབྲིང |

## [?] (0)

There are none. Every syllable was decided on the image, or the image and the witness agree.

Close calls not marked [?]:
- 70.5 སྤྲད་ཀྱང: the head of ད runs into ཀྱ with no visible tsheg. A fused tsheg cannot be ruled out, so the witness's tsheg is kept. If the drafter reads it as absent: `# fix: ངོ་སྤྲདཀྱང => ངོ་སྤྲད་ཀྱང`.
- 72.1 ཅིང་༔: a 3×4 px bump stands on the top-left of the ༔ ring (x 1713–1717, rows 123–125), one or two rows above the ring itself. It is read as a fused tsheg, as the witness has it. If it is taken as part of the ring, the reading is ཅིང༔ and no fix is needed.
- 71.3 ཞག་བདུན: the gap between ག and བ is about 4 px with no free dot. The tsheg is taken as fused (witness).
- 70.5 ད versus ང (see the table) rests on the tail length in direct pixel comparison. Certainty is high, not absolute.

- Line-join tshegs: the joins 69.4→69.5, 70.2→70.3, 70.4→70.5, 71.2→71.3 and 71.3→71.4. None of these joins crosses a page-opening ornament. The joins that do (68.5→69.1 and 70.5→71.1) are not affected: 70.5 ends མི་ with a tsheg. Whether 68.5 ends with a tsheg is Reader B's report.
- Ligature: 71.1 ཚོགྶ (written གས).

## Suspected misprints

1. 70.4 **ཐ་མའི་ཡང་ཐམ་མི་ཡུལ**: no tsheg between ཐ and མ. ×10: the head bars join and there is no room for a dot. The witness also typed ཐམ. Only ཐ་མ makes sense ("the lowest of the low"). Certainty: moderate to high (it could be a fused or worn tsheg). Proposed fix: `ཡང་ཐམ་མི => ཡང་ཐ་མ་མི` (rule 5b, print's reading in the note).
2. 71.1 **ཞག་བདུན་པལ་དག་བ**: no tsheg between པ and ལ. ×7: the letters stand side by side with no dot, while every other tsheg in this stretch of the line is visible. The witness also has པལ. Only པ་ལ makes sense ("on the seventh day"; compare 71.3 ཞག་བདུན་པ་ལ). Certainty: moderate to high. Proposed fix: `བདུན་པལ་དག => བདུན་པ་ལ་དག`.
3. 69.3 **མདུན་པ་རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་གཏོད**, which may be meant as འདུན་པ ("aspiration"; the other recension has འདུན་པ). མདུན་པ is attested as a variant spelling, and "turn [your] front one-pointedly towards" also reads. Kept, note only.
4. 70.2 **ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱང** against the other recension's ཐ་མས་ཀྱང. The print's sequence is (unnamed best) … འབྲིང … ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱང ("even all [of them], by the power of the pure prayer…"). It may originally have been ཐ་མས, "even the lowest", completing a rab/'bring/tha ma triad. But the print's reading makes sense and is clearly cut. Kept, note only.

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: སངས་རྒྱའོ, དག་བ, འཁྱམས་དུ, བོས་ལ, ཀྱེ beside ཀྱཻ, ཅིག for ཞིག.

- 70.4: print ཞི་བ་ལ་གསལ་བར (with ལ); other recension གསར་བར. Print ཤས་ཆེ་བ་གཅིག; other recension འགྲོ་བ་ཤས་ཆེ་བ་ཞིག. Same.
- 70.4: print ཐ་མའི་ཡང་ཐ(་)མ་མི་ཡུལ་དུ ("in the human world"); other recension ཐ་མ་མའི་ཡུལ་ལ (a slip there). Same.
- 70.5: print ངོ་སྤྲད་ཀྱང་མི་འཕྲོད་པར; other recension ཀྱང་མ་འཕྲོད་པར. Same.
- 71.1: print ཞག་བདུན་པ་ལ་དག་བ་མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ཀྱི་ཞིང་ནས; other recension …ཞིང་ཁམས་ནས. Same.
- 71.2: print འོད་ལམ་ཀྱང; other recension འོད་ལམ་གྱིས་ཀྱང. Same.
- 71.3: **print དེའི་དུས་སུ་རང་ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ནི ("at that time the self-introduction is"); other recension ཡང་ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ནི ("again, the introduction is")**.
- 71.3: print བོས་ལ; other recension འབོད་ལ. Same.
- 71.4: print འོད་ལྔ་ཁྲ་བོ་འཆར ("the five multicoloured lights arise"); other recension འོད་ཁྲ་བོ་ཤར. Close.
- 71.4: **print དེའི་དུས་སུ་མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ཀྱི་ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ༔ … བསུ་བ་ལ་འོང ("the knowledge-holders come to meet [you] in the Khecara realm"); other recension དག་པ་མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ཀྱི་ཞིང་ཁམས་ནས ("from the pure Khecara realm")**.
- 71.5: **print འཇའ་དང་འོད་དུ་འཐིབ་པའི་དབུས་སུ ("in the midst of a dense mass of rainbow and light"); other recension འཇའ་དང་འོད་དུ་ཐིམ་པའི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་དབུས་སུ ("in the centre of a maṇḍala dissolving into rainbow and light")**.
- 72.1: **print གྲི་གུག་དང་ཐོད་ཁྲག་འཛིན་ཅིང ("holding a curved knife and a skull of blood"); other recension གྲི་གུག་དང་ཐོད་ཁྲག་གི་གར་མཛད་ཅིང ("dancing with …")**. For the eastern vidyādhara the witness has the dance formula (…གི་གར་མཛད་ཅིང, p. 72.3, beyond this part).
- 72.2: print བལྟ་སྟངས, ཅིག; other recension ལྟ་སྟངས, ཞིག. Same.

## Proposed name

`# name: Day six closes with the prayer to the five families; day seven, the knowledge-holders appear`

The part (pp. 63–72.2) runs from day six's light-paths of the four wisdoms combined, through the six impure lights and the prayer, to its result for the best, middling and all. It then opens day seven: the vidyādharas from Khecara with the animal-realm light, and the first of them, Padma Gar gyi dbang phyug. A shorter form: `# name: The prayer of the five families; day seven, the knowledge-holders`.
